hero_deck: Lima Airport had never charged international transfer passengers a fee. I designed the web channel to collect it and handed it over.
hero_role1: Roles — Internal consultant · UX/UI designer · CX designer
hero_role3: Scope — Planning → UX/UI design → prototyping → evaluation → handoff
hero_rv_txt: A tourist lands in Lima and connects to another international flight. At the new terminal they owe a fee the airport had never charged, and no channel existed to collect it. Ten areas across four central offices each held a piece of the problem. As the internal consultant from the Innovation area, I took part in planning and contributed deliverables, designed the web payment flow, evaluated it and handed it to the team that built it. TUUA Transfer runs today, charging 130,000+ international transfer passengers a month.
act0_verdict: A new fee, with no world precedent.
act0_lede: Follow a connection, then compare the two ways to pay.
act0_rv1: Jorge Chávez. Lima's international airport, run by the private operator Lima Airport Partners, where I worked.
act0_rv2: International transfer passenger. A passenger who arrives in Lima on an international flight and connects to another international flight.
act0_rv3: TUUA. Tarifa Unificada de Uso de Aeropuerto, the airport-use fee. TUUA Transfer is the one charged for the services these passengers use while they board.
act0_pos_cap: Two ways to pay the fee
act0_pos_r1_web: A site exclusive to collect this fee
act0_pos_r1_staff: Three staffed points of sale in the terminal
act0_pos_r2_web: A QR code by email, shown at the eGate
act0_pos_r2_staff: A bar-code sticker on the boarding pass
act0_pos_r3_web: Skipping the queues at rush hours
act0_pos_r3_staff: Paying in person, with staff on hand
act0_pos_btn: One fee, two ways to pay
act0_pos_txt: A physical-digital model. The fee is collected inside the airport, during the connection. Three staffed points carry most payments; a web channel, built only for this fee, lets passengers skip the queues at peak hours. Both end at the same eGate.
act1_verdict: A fee with no way to collect it.
act1_lede: Step through how a contract promise became a critical income stream.
act1_t1_x: LAP begins operating Jorge Chávez under concession with Peruvian State.
act1_t2_x: Contract amendment allows transfer fees upon delivery of new terminal.
act1_t3_x: Construction delayed for years while the State releases the land it needs.
act1_t4_x: The fee becomes chargeable, but no mechanism exists to collect it.
act1_t5_x: LAP negotiated Airlines could collect the fee inside the ticket.
act1_t6_x: Finance's answer: collect the fee inside the airport itself.
act1_s1_p: Charged today, on a platform Lima Airport's IT runs.
act1_s2_p: Left uncollected for each day without collection channel.
act1_s3_p: The State takes 46.511% as royalty: ≈ $20,300 a day.
act1_est_txt: 130,000 × USD 10.05 ÷ 30 days. USD 10.05 is the fee before 18% IGV, which makes it $11.86. Lima Airport keeps 53.489%; the State takes 46.511% as royalty under the concession. An estimate at today's volume, not a measured loss.

act6_verdict: The platform is live, it isn't mine, and the gap is public.
act6_lede: A year later, I reviewed the live platform against my proposal. Select any step to compare the two.
act6_method: Public, unauthenticated pages only. No transaction was submitted, no session was captured, and no data was collected beyond what any visitor sees.
act6_hint: Select a step in either flow to compare it with the other.
act6_n_data: Reordered, not removed. Personal-data capture moved from my first screen to the live flow's fourth, after the flight lookup. I read the reordering as intuitive and do not contest it.
act6_n_val: No counterpart before payment. None of the four public screens asks for an email code.
act6_n_fee: $11.86, a screen earlier. The live fee appears on the flight-details screen, a full screen earlier than I proposed, and matches in both places it appears. Fee-setting was never my decision.
act6_n_ticket: Beyond the boundary. The review stopped before payment, so the live ticket was not observed.
act6_n_home: An entry page first. The live flow opens on a homepage that explains the fee before the first step.
act6_n_elig: A click instead of a check. Eligibility is a self-declaration, "Soy ese tipo de pasajero", where the technical scope specified an automatic agreement check. To my own knowledge of the build, that check was never implemented as written; the review could not see past its boundary to confirm it.
act6_n_ctrl: Where the review stops. Public, unauthenticated pages only: one control short of paying, with no transaction submitted.
act6_s1_p: The same in both of its appearances.
act6_s2_p: Setting the fee was never my decision.
act6_sev_cap: Six findings from the review, by severity
act6_fr_txt: A heading that asks for more than the form does. A screen headed "Ingresa tus datos personales y de tu vuelo" whose only fields are flight data.
act6_k1_x: The design, prototype, evaluation and handoff of a platform live today.
act6_k2_x: Its build, deployment and operation belong to others.
act6_k3_x: One major and five minor, recorded for whoever runs the platform.
act3_notice: TUUA Transfer. I understand the platform's mechanism and contributed to its UX/UI design — not its development, deployment or operation.
